description: Resource Description Framework (W3C): knowledge as subject-predicate-object triples with global IRIs. Graphs from different sources merge by union.
Internationalized Resource Identifier: a global identifier such as `https://schema.org/worksFor`, so the same term means the same thing across datasets.
Common RDF serializations: Turtle is compact and readable; JSON-LD embeds linked data in JSON, widely used on web pages.
Web Ontology Language (W3C): rich class and property logic for reasoners that infer new facts under the open-world assumption.
Shapes Constraint Language (W3C): validates RDF data against shapes and reports violations. The closed-world validator of the RDF stack.
The W3C query language for RDF: triple patterns with variables, property paths for transitive queries.
ISO/IEC 39075:2024, the ISO standard query language for property graphs, drawing on Cypher and other graph languages.
Business entities, metrics and dimensions defined once (formula, filters, grain, owner) and served to BI tools, APIs and AI agents.
